summary.title: 为可见光吸热涂料的光谱选择性表面设计吸收膜：在 400-700 nm 可见波
summary.question: 为可见光吸热涂料的光谱选择性表面设计吸收膜：在 400-700 nm 可见波段吸收率尽可能高（反射率尽可能低），而在 700-2000 nm 近红外波段反射率尽可能高以抑制热输入。请在空气入射、铝基底条件下，仅使用 HfO2 和 SiO2 与金属 Cr 设计一个平面多层膜，膜系总层数不超过 20 层。

problem.compatibility_reason: The request specifies a planar multilayer film with isotropic linear materials under plane-wave illumination, which fits the TMM solver scope.
materials: Allowed film materials: HfO2, SiO2, Cr

metrics.rationale: User explicitly requests '在 400-700 nm 可见波段吸收率尽可能高' (absorptance as high as possible in 400-700 nm visible band) for heat absorption
User explicitly requests '在 700-2000 nm 近红外波段反射率尽可能高以抑制热输入' (reflectance as high as possible in 700-2000 nm near-infrared band to suppress heat input)

scoring.metric_rationale: These two metrics directly capture the spectral selectivity requirement stated in the user's request: high absorption in the visible band (400-700 nm) for heat collection, and high reflection in the near-infrared band (700-2000 nm) to suppress thermal load. I chose mean metrics rather than worst_case because the user says '尽可能高' (as high as possible) indicating average performance across each band is the optimization target. I deliberately did not add a separate reflectance metric for the visible band because for an opaque system with Al substrate, high absorption inherently implies low reflection, so adding it would be redundant and dilute the scoring weight. I also did not use band_emissivity_contrast as a single metric because the user's language emphasizes both bands separately, and two explicit metrics give clearer control over each spectral region's performance.
scoring.formula_rationale: The user requires two complementary spectral goals: maximizing absorption in the visible band (400-700 nm) and maximizing reflectance in the near-infrared band (700-2000 nm). Both metrics are marked as 'maximize', so both are added positively. No weighting coefficients are applied because the request treats both spectral regions as equally critical for the selective surface function (absorbing visible light while rejecting infrared heat). A simple sum ensures that improving performance in either band increases the total score, reflecting the dual objective without arbitrary prioritization.

routes.title: DBR-Backed Chromium Absorber
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A distributed Bragg reflector of HfO2/SiO2 pairs beneath a thin Cr layer will reflect near-infrared light back through the Cr for secondary absorption while the Cr at the air interface absorbs visible light directly, achieving high visible absorptance with high IR reflectance.
routes.design_principle: DBR structures create high reflectivity bands through constructive interference of reflections from alternating high/low index layers. Placing Cr at the air interface captures visible light on first pass, while the DBR reflects IR and any transmitted visible back through Cr for additional absorption opportunities.
routes.topology: Air / Cr / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / Al substrate
known_risks: Cr may absorb some IR reducing reflectance
DBR band edge may not align perfectly with 700 nm cutoff
Visible absorption may be limited by single Cr pass

The Al substrate provides inherent NIR reflectivity that the stack enhances.
